I will still farm the 2.6 mu the same wheat-maize rotation, because that is what my land suits and I know how to manage it. I do not like changing too much at my age. I will start from what I did last year, then adjust a little by looking at fertilizer price, water, and what the neighbors around me are doing. On this small piece of land, every bag costs money, but if I cut fertilizer too hard and the yield falls, that hurts more than wasting a little. I have well water, so I will not let the crop suffer for lack of moisture. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put more fertilizer at the start, then topdress once when it is growing strong. Wheat is my careful crop, so I will water about 3 times if the season is normal and spray 2 times if I see aphids or disease. After wheat harvest, I will plant maize quickly, use hybrid seed, give enough nitrogen, and water 2 times in a normal year. I will keep the field in rotary tillage because my land is small and that is easier for me to handle. If weather is normal, I will aim for steady yield, not the very highest yield, because I am farming mostly with family labor and I want a safe harvest.
